newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Westinghouse Asia to develop Cambodia power plants.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse Asia to develop Cambodia power plants.

text.p: Westinghouse Asia will develop four independent power plants in Cambodia under a $7 million deal approved by the government on Tuesday, officials said.
Westinghouse Asia will soon begin work on technical studies on three plants in the northwestern province of Banteay Meanchey and one in Takeo province in the south, Industry Ministry officials said.

The company will then be expected to develop the power plants, including distribution grids, pending discussion on exact terms of operation, said Kreal Khon, director of the ministry's energy department.

Secretary of State for Industry Ith Praing said the facilities would probably be between one to three megawatts, though an official with Power Investment Group said at least one of the facilities might be five megawatts.

Calling the deal "good for Cambodia," Ith Praing noted that blue-chip investors such as Westinghouse were symbolically important to Cambodia, where few multinational corporations have dared to venture.
Tep Rithivit, whose Power Investment Group firm represents Westinghouse Asia in Cambodia, called the project an example for multinationals in the future.
"It is an opportunity for Cambodia to work with an able, well-known firm," he said.

Cambodian infrastructure, particularly electricity, is in poor condition after years of civil war. But recent aid in the sector and deals such as that inked with Westinghouse are expected to improve the situation.
